Deployment Strategist (DS) & Senior Deployment Strategist (Sr. DS)

About MelodyArc

MelodyArc is building the orchestration layer for enterprise service work — where rules, people, and AI collaborate to get complex operations done reliably at scale. Our orchestration core (the Point Engine) enables teams to configure agentic AI Operators that execute work end-to-end while leveraging existing business logic and human-in-the-loop workflows. Learn More.

Role Overview

As a Deployment Strategist, you are the owner of the customer's outcome. You take a signed customer from kickoff through a production deployment that is live, adopted, and demonstrably delivering value — and you own everything non-engineering required to get there. You are the "product manager for the field" paired with client single point of contact: you define what gets built and why, you relentlessly manage scope and timeline, and you drive the engagement to a successful landing in production.

This is a delivery-first role. You will spend most of your time defining process and use cases, scoping deployments, authoring the requirements that guide the build, running the engagement as a hands-on project owner, acting as the primary QA tester for the customer's solution, driving adoption after launch, and communicating financial ROI. You partner with our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), who own the how — the deep technical build — while you own the what, the why, and the path to a landed outcome.

Our best Deployment Strategists are unusually resourceful operators who combine strategic business experience in large organizations, product-style thinking, executive communication, and a "whatever it takes to ship" mindset. You are comfortable in a customer's data and workflows, you can read and configure aspects of the Point Engine, but are not expected to build production software. You know exactly when to pull in an FDE.

How This Role Relates to the Forward Deployed Engineering

The Deployment Strategist and the Forward Deployed Engineer are partners on every engagement. The split is deliberate:

  • Deployment Strategist owns the problem--sometimes even supporting the proof of concept build pre-sign--the requirements, scope, timeline, stakeholder management, QA, and adoption. The DS is technical enough to configure the platform, write basic queries, map data, and validate solutions hands-on — but does not own the production codebase.
  • Forward Deployed Engineer owns the technical build: custom integrations, complex configuration, and production-grade engineering.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end delivery of customer deployments — from kickoff through a live, adopted, value-proven production solution — as the single accountable owner of the outcome.
  • Scope each deployment: define the minimum viable solution, success criteria, milestones, and timeline, and translate the customer's business problem into a clear requirements document (PRD) that guides the FDE build team.
  • Run the engagement as a hands-on project owner: prioritize the backlog, manage scope relentlessly, sequence milestones, and drive day-to-day execution alongside FDEs.
  • Act as the primary QA tester for the customer's solution — validate that what is built actually solves the problem before it reaches the customer.
  • Configure the MelodyArc platform directly where appropriate (workflow configuration, data mapping, queries, light scripting) and know when to hand deeper technical work to an FDE.
  • Manage all stakeholder communication, from frontline operators to senior sponsors, and act as the escalation owner who unblocks technical, political, and process issues.
  • Own the launch: run the go-live, manage the cutover, and drive the solution from launch to full adoption by capturing user feedback, iterating, and proving the defined business value.
  • Scope the ongoing support and maintenance plan, create customer-facing documentation and enablement, and ensure a clean handoff to steady-state.
  • Partner with Sales and Account teams on discovery and value scoping for new and expansion opportunities, drawing on your trusted-advisor relationship with the customer.

Basic Qualifications

  • 4+ years (DS) or 7+ years (Sr. DS) of client-facing delivery experience in roles such as deployment strategy, technical program/project management, solutions/implementation consulting, or product management at a technology company or top-tier consultancy.
  • Demonstrated ownership of complex projects end-to-end: scoping, sequencing milestones, managing scope, and shipping to production or launch.
  • Strong product and systems thinking: able to translate an ambiguous business problem into clear requirements, success criteria, and a prioritized plan.
  • Technical fluency: comfortable working hands-on in data and workflow tooling — reading and writing SQL, mapping data, configuring software, and validating solutions — without requiring an engineer for routine tasks.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the executive presence to build trust and drive decisions with senior stakeholders.
  • A relentless, hands-on execution mentality — willing to do the unglamorous work required to land a deployment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience deploying enterprise software, data, or AI/ML solutions into production at named accounts.
  • Experience writing PRDs and running an agile delivery process with an engineering team.
  • Experience with value-based scoping (ROI) and quantifying business outcomes for senior stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with customer service operations, contact-center workflows, or business-process operations.
  • Comfort with light scripting, APIs, and integration concepts (enough to scope and validate, not to build production systems).
  • Prior experience in a "founder," "builder," or early-team capacity at a high-growth startup.

Location

Remote (United States). Some travel to customer sites may be required.

Equal Opportunity

MelodyArc is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by law. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, let your recruiter know and we'll work with you.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $150,000–$185,000. This is a good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay on hire; where an offer lands depends on experience, skills, and work location. As an early-stage company, total compensation also includes equity. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, flexible paid time off, and paid parental leave.

Salary: $150,000 – $185,000 / year

jobs.title: Lead Master Trainer & Director of Training Quality
jobs.excerpt: GPS Lead Master Trainer & Director of Training QualityPosition OverviewThe GPS Lead Master Trainer & Director of Training Quality is responsible for the delivery of GPS trainings, including ensuring the quality, consistency, and fidelity of the GPS Group Peer Support model across all GPS trainings, facilitators, trainers, and learning materials.
jobs.description:
GPS Lead Master Trainer & Director of Training Quality

Position Overview

The GPS Lead Master Trainer & Director of Training Quality is responsible for the delivery of GPS trainings, including ensuring the quality, consistency, and fidelity of the GPS Group Peer Support model across all GPS trainings, facilitators, trainers, and learning materials.

This is a senior training leadership role for someone who is an exceptional trainer and facilitator and can quickly develop a deep understanding of the GPS model, teach it with excellence, and ensure that others deliver it with the same level of quality and fidelity.

The Lead Master Trainer provides day-to-day leadership, supervision, coaching,and quality oversight to GPS trainers and facilitators; actively leads GPS trainings; provides real-time guidance and decision-making related to training delivery, facilitator support, and model fidelity; ensures training materials remain accurate, current, and organized; and helps GPS build the training capacity needed to grow while protecting the integrity of the model.

The Lead Master Trainer also ensures training materials remain accurate, current, organized, and consistently implemented and helps GPS build the trainer and facilitator capacity needed to grow while protecting the integrity of the model.

The person in this role serves as a keeper of the GPS model, providing the leadership, structure, and expertise needed to ensure that as GPS expands, the quality and consistency of our work remain strong.

What You'll Lead

Training Quality & Fidelity

  • Own quality and fidelity standards for all GPS training and facilitation.
  • Ensure the GPS model is taught and facilitated consistently across programs, populations, trainers, and facilitators.
  • Observe and assess trainings and facilitation.
  • Identify quality concerns and ensure appropriate coaching, remediation, and follow-up.
  • Develop systems for ongoing quality assurance and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure that growth and expansion do not compromise the integrity of the GPS model.
  • Ensure all trainers and facilitators understand, practice, and consistently follow GPS safety protocols, professional boundaries, and escalation procedures.
  • Provide leadership and consultation when challenging or concerning situations arise during trainings or support groups, ensuring they are handled appropriately and consistently.
  • Coach trainers and facilitators in navigating difficult group dynamics, participant concerns, and other complex situations while maintaining the integrity and safety of the GPS model.

Master Training

  • Serve as a senior/master trainer for GPS Facilitator Training and other GPS professional learning programs.
  • Model exceptional GPS training and facilitation practices.
  • Train and develop new GPS trainers and master trainers.
  • Determine trainer readiness and support trainers as they progress toward independent delivery.
  • Lead train-the-trainer activities as GPS expands its training capacity and team.
  • Actively lead GPS Facilitator Trainings and other assigned GPS training programs as a primary trainer.
  • Provide real-time leadership during trainings, including making decisions related to delivery, facilitator roles, participant needs, and model fidelity.
  • Step into training or facilitation roles when needed to ensure continuity and quality.

Trainer & Facilitator Leadership

  • Provide leadership, supervision, coaching, and ongoing professional development to GPS trainers and facilitators.
  • Provide direct day-to-day supervision and support to GPS trainers and facilitators.
  • Lead or oversee pre-session planning and post-session debrief meetings, ensuring roles, expectations, session flow, and responsibilities are clear.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for routine trainer and facilitator questions, concerns, and real-time decisions.
  • Hold trainers and facilitators accountable to established GPS protocols, expectations, and model-fidelity standards.
  • Address performance concerns and provide clear, timely feedback, coaching, and follow-up.
  • Establish clear expectations and performance standards.
  • Create opportunities for trainers and facilitators to strengthen their skills.
  • Identify performance or fidelity concerns early and develop plans to address them.
  • Build a strong, collaborative community of trainers and facilitators committed to learning and excellence.

Curriculum & Training Materials

  • Maintain training-quality and fidelity oversight of GPS curricula, facilitator materials, trainer guides, presentations, session outlines, manuals, and related resources.
  • Develop and/or review session outlines and other implementation materials needed for consistent program delivery.
  • Monitor how curricula and materials are used in practice to ensure fidelity to the GPS model.
  • Provide feedback to the Curriculum Director based on trainer, facilitator, and participant experience and identify opportunities for clarification, revision, or improvement.
  • Identify content or material changes needed based on facilitator feedback, participant experience, or fidelity concerns and collaborate with program leadership and subject-matter experts on approved revisions.
  • Ensure trainers and facilitators are always working from the correct and most current materials.
  • Maintain clear version control and an organized system for all training materials.
  • Work with the Curriculum Director, program leadership, and subject-matter experts to implement approved curriculum and material changes.
  • Work with the Curriculum Director, program leadership, and subject-matter experts to implement approved curriculum and material changes.
  • Ensure approved changes are clearly communicated, understood, and consistently implemented across the training and facilitation team.

Growth & Capacity Building

  • Help GPS build the trainer and facilitator capacity required for national growth.
  • Identify, develop, and mentor strong trainers and facilitators.
  • Develop scalable systems for onboarding, evaluating, coaching, and supporting trainers and facilitators.
  • Help determine staffing and trainer capacity for new programs and partnerships.
  • Support adaptation of GPS programming for new populations and settings while protecting core model fidelity.

Quality Systems & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and maintain SOPs related to training quality, trainer development, facilitation, and fidelity.
  • Establish clear processes for observation, feedback, coaching, and performance improvement.
  • Track recurring issues and recommend improvements to training, materials, and systems.
  • Partner with program leadership to ensure participant feedback and evaluation findings inform continuous improvement.

Success in This Role

You'll be successful if:

  • GPS trainings consistently reflect the quality and values of the GPS model.
  • Trainers and facilitators understand exactly what excellent GPS delivery looks like.
  • New trainers and facilitators are developed effectively and supported to succeed.
  • Quality concerns are identified and addressed before they become larger problems.
  • Training materials are current, accurate, organized, and consistently used.
  • GPS can expand its training capacity without sacrificing quality or fidelity.
  • Trainers and facilitators experience strong leadership, coaching, and professional development.
  • Leadership has confidence that GPS programs are being delivered consistently and at a high level.

Qualifications

  • Exceptional trainer, facilitator, and leader — able to engage, inspire, coach, and develop others.
  • Ability to train diverse communities and professional audiences — while adapting their approach without losing fidelity to GPS.
  • Cultural humility — ability to build trust and connection across different backgrounds, identities, lived experiences, and professional roles.
  • Leadership of trainers and facilitators — including giving direct feedback and holding people to high standards.
  • Significant experience delivering and/or overseeing training, facilitation, adult learning, professional development, or related programs.
  • Exceptional training and facilitation skills.
  • Experience directly supervising or managing trainers, facilitators, instructors, or similar teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to make sound real-time decisions in training, facilitation, or program-delivery environments. Strong understanding of adult learning and experiential education.
  • Experience establishing and monitoring quality or fidelity standards.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and feedback skills.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Ability to organize and maintain complex curricula and training materials.
  • Ability to balance fidelity to a model with thoughtful adaptation and continuous improvement.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.

Preferred Experience

Experience with:

  • GPS Group Peer Support or similar peer-support models.
  • Trauma-informed approaches.
  • Train-the-trainer programs.
  • Trainer certification or competency assessment.
  • Continuing education or professional development.
  • Healthcare, behavioral health, nonprofit, or community-based programs.
  • Learning management systems and online learning.
  • Scaling training programs across multiple organizations, communities, or geographic regions.
  • Personal or professional experience that provides meaningful understanding of the communities GPS serves, including people in recovery, perinatal populations, healthcare workers, and other diverse communities.
  • Advanced degree in mental health, behavioral health, social work, psychology, counseling, or a related field preferred.
  • Bilingual or multilingual (Spanish, Haitian Creole, Portuguese, Vietnamese, Russian)

GPS Facilitator Certification or GPS Trainer experience strongly preferred. Candidates with relevant experience who are not trained yet must be willing to complete intensive GPS Training and demonstrate mastery of the model.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who is an exceptional teacher, trainer, coach, and leader—someone who can hold a high bar for quality while helping people grow toward it.

This person should be able to see both the individual trainer in front of them and the larger system GPS needs to build. They should care deeply about the integrity of the GPS model, be comfortable giving clear and constructive feedback, and be excited about developing the people and systems that will allow GPS to grow without losing what makes our work powerful.

Salary: $85,000 – $100,000 / year

We are looking for a Mid-Level Web Engineer with strong React and Node.js experience to join an engineering team focused on Performance Marketing, Growth and Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO).

The team builds the technology that supports Organic Search and Growth initiatives, helping ensure content is discoverable and cited across both traditional search engines and emerging AI-driven search experiences, including Google Search, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Mode.

  • Build and develop scalable web applications and pages using React and Node.js;

  • Develop and consume APIs and integrate services where required;
  • Test solutions across different browsers and devices and identify technical issues;
  • Use Git-based source control and modern development workflows;
  • Contribute ideas for improving applications, development processes and the way the team delivers solutions at scale;
  • Participate in Agile ceremonies, technical discussions and project planning;
  • Take ownership of assigned tasks and deliver high-quality solutions within agreed timelines.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or any related technical field.
  • Strong professional experience in modern web development;
  • Strong proficiency in React.js and its core principles;
  • Strong proficiency in Node.js and experience building or supporting server-side web applications and services;
  • Strong knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML5 and CSS3;
  • Experience building maintainable, scalable and reusable web solutions;
  • Good understanding of modern frontend development practices, tooling and build processes;
  • Experience working with RESTful APIs and integrating frontend and backend services;
  • Good understanding of Git and collaborative software development workflows;
  • Experience implementing responsive and cross-browser web solutions;
  • Ability to write clean, maintainable and well-structured code;
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills;
  • A curious and proactive mindset, with the confidence to investigate problems and suggest improvements;
  • Comfortable working on process-related initiatives alongside core software development;
  • Experience working within Agile and cross-functional teams;
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

AWESOME BUT NOT REQUIRED:

  • Previous experience working within SEO, Growth Engineering or Performance Marketing teams;
  • Understanding of Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) and how AI-driven search is changing content discovery;
  • Experience with Content Management Systems (CMS);
  • Experience with Umbraco or similar CMS platforms;
  • Knowledge of structured data, schema markup and search-engine optimisation;
  • Experience developing large-scale, content-heavy websites or platforms with thousands of pages;
  • Familiarity with optimising web architecture and content for both traditional search engines and AI-driven search experiences.

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU?

  • Be part of our collegial environment where responsibility and authority are shared equally amongst colleagues and help create our company culture
  • A culture in which we don’t criticise failure but ensure we learn from our mistakes
  • An Agile environment where your ideas are welcome
  • The possibility to grow and experience different projects
  • Ongoing Training & Mentoring
  • The possibility to travel

Beacon Nonprofit empowers mission-driven founders as they navigate the nonprofit journey, from formation through compliance and growth.

SnapMailbox provides virtual mailbox and mail management solutions for entrepreneurs, remote businesses, global remote workers, and distributed teams who need secure, flexible mail handling.

360 Legal Forms provides individuals, families, and businesses with access to a comprehensive library of attorney-vetted legal documents.

  • Conduct a structured post-signature handoff, including complete documentation of business needs, contracted terms, timelines, stakeholders, and commitments made during the sales process.

  • Provide reliable pipeline forecasts and monitor pipeline coverage, conversion rates, sales-cycle progress, and performance against assigned goals.
  • Share market feedback, customer needs, competitive insights, and sales trends with Sales, Marketing, Product, and leadership.
  • Represent the company professionally at customer meetings, webinars, conferences, trade shows, and industry events.

What You’ll Need

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Sales, Communications, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
  • Three to seven or more years of experience in account executive, business development, partnerships, channel sales, strategic alliances, or consultative B2B sales.

  • Strong cold-calling, outbound prospecting, consultative selling, presentation, objection-handling, and negotiation skills.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role will be measured by:

Compensation

jobs.description:
Processo de seleção desenvolvido pela matteria

Localização e modo de trabalho

Residência fixa em uma das capitais da Amazônia Legal brasileira - Remoto

Quem somos

A missão da The Nature Conservancy (TNC) é proteger as terras e as águas das quais toda a vida depende. Como uma organização baseada na ciência, criamos soluções inovadoras e práticas para os desafios mais difíceis do mundo, para que possamos criar um mundo no qual as pessoas e a natureza prosperem. Estamos enraizados em nossa Missão e guiados por nossos Valores, que incluem o Compromisso com a Diversidade e o Respeito às Pessoas, Comunidades e Culturas. Seja desenvolvimento de carreira, horários flexíveis ou uma missão gratificante, há muitas razões para amar a vida na TNC. Quer ter uma visão melhor da TNC? Confira nossa conta no instagram e o Relatório Anual 2024, além da #tncbrasil no LinkedIn.

Nosso objetivo é cultivar um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo para que todos os nossos colegas em todo o mundo sintam um sentimento de pertencimento e que suas contribuições únicas para nossa missão sejam valorizadas. Sabemos que só alcançaremos nossa Missão contratando e engajando uma força de trabalho diversificada que reflita as comunidades em que trabalhamos. Além dos requisitos em nossas postagens, reconhecemos que as pessoas vêm com talento e experiências fora do trabalho. A diversidade de experiências e habilidades combinadas com paixão são a chave para a inovação e uma cultura de inclusão! Por favor, inscreva-se - adoraríamos ouvir de você. Para citar o que inúmeros membros da equipe da TNC dizem: “você se juntará por causa da nossa missão e ficará por nossas pessoas”.

Nosso impacto

  • 71 milhões de hectares: impacto positivo almejado até 2030, com foco em conservação e aprimoramento da gestão.

  • 187 mil km de rios: extensão para a qual a TNC Brasil busca promover soluções e políticas públicas de conservação até 2030.

  • 369 milhões de toneladas de CO₂: volume de emissões que a organização pretende capturar ou contribuir para reduzir até 2030.

  • 3,8 milhões de pessoas: público que a TNC Brasil pretende apoiar, com atenção especial a povos tradicionais e comunidades indígenas, ampliando sua participação em espaços decisórios e sua liderança na gestão dos territórios.

Na Amazônia, exemplos recentes ajudam a dimensionar essa atuação: um projeto de Pagamento por Serviços Ambientais na Terra do Meio envolve 14 territórios coletivos, 3 mil pessoas e 10 milhões de hectares sob proteção de uso sustentável.

Propósito do cargo

Liderar a estratégia da TNC na Amazônia Brasileira a partir de uma visão sistêmica do território, conciliando conservação e desenvolvimento socioeconômico. O desafio será conectar diferentes agendas, atores e investimentos para transformar estratégias em resultados concretos e escaláveis, capazes de manter a floresta em pé, promover uma produção responsável e gerar valor para as pessoas e comunidades da Amazônia.

Principais responsabilidades

  • Acompanhar e implementar a estratégia e a Teoria da Mudança da TNC para a Amazônia Brasileira, traduzindo a visão institucional em prioridades, iniciativas e resultados mensuráveis.

  • Liderar um portfólio amplo e diverso, conectando agendas de produção agropecuária sustentável, proteção e valorização da floresta em pé, povos indígenas e comunidades tradicionais, clima, mecanismos financeiros e políticas públicas.

  • Assegurar capacidade de implementação e entrega, transformando estratégias em resultados concretos, monitorando avanços e adaptando planos diante de mudanças de contexto.

  • Promover uma visão de desenvolvimento socioeconômico da Amazônia, articulando conservação e produção responsável e identificando alavancas econômicas capazes de valorizar a floresta em pé.

  • Identificar oportunidades para ampliar iniciativas bem-sucedidas, superando a lógica de projetos-piloto e promovendo soluções com potencial de transformação sistêmica e atuação em larga escala.

  • Construir e fortalecer relações estratégicas com governos estaduais e federal, setor privado, instituições financeiras, produtores, academia, organizações da sociedade civil, financiadores, povos indígenas, quilombolas, extrativistas e outras comunidades tradicionais.

  • Influenciar políticas públicas, estruturas de governança e processos de tomada de decisão relevantes para o desenvolvimento sustentável da Amazônia.

  • Liderar e apoiar a captação de recursos no Brasil e internacionalmente, mantendo um pipeline consistente de oportunidades e relacionamento estratégico com financiadores.

  • Supervisionar a gestão financeira e orçamentária de um portfólio de grande porte, assegurando uso eficiente dos recursos, sustentabilidade financeira e conformidade institucional.

  • Liderar gestores e equipes multidisciplinares, fortalecendo estruturas, responsabilidades, autonomia, accountability e capacidades técnicas e gerenciais.

  • Estimular integração e sinergia entre diferentes frentes de atuação, evitando silos e promovendo circulação de contexto e informação para qualificar a tomada de decisão.

  • Manter e fortalecer a agenda de diversidade, equidade e inclusão dentro da unidade, incorporando-a à liderança e à gestão da equipe.

  • Representar institucionalmente a TNC em fóruns, negociações e espaços estratégicos nacionais e internacionais.

Requisitos e competências para trabalhar conosco

Educação

  • Formação superior completa em áreas relacionadas à gestão de recursos naturais, políticas públicas, economia ou áreas afins. Pós-graduação em áreas correlatas será considerada desejável.

Experiência

  • Mínimo de 10 anos de experiência profissional em posições relacionadas a desenvolvimento socioeconômico, gestão de recursos naturais, políticas públicas, conservação ou áreas correlatas, com trajetória relevante em contextos complexos e de grande escala.

  • Experiência robusta na definição e implementação de estratégias, com responsabilidade por portfólios complexos, priorização de iniciativas, gestão de riscos e entrega de resultados mensuráveis.

  • Experiência comprovada na liderança de gestores e equipes multidisciplinares, incluindo desenvolvimento de talentos, estruturação de equipes e gestão de desempenho.

  • Trajetória de articulação multissetorial, estabelecendo relações e conduzindo negociações complexas com governos, setor privado, organizações da sociedade civil, comunidades, financiadores e outros atores estratégicos.

  • Experiência em relações governamentais e políticas públicas, incluindo capacidade de influenciar agendas, processos decisórios e condições institucionais necessárias para alcançar resultados em escala.

  • Experiência na gestão financeira e orçamentária de programas de grande porte, combinando visão estratégica com capacidade de acompanhamento da execução.

  • Experiência em captação de recursos e relacionamento com financiadores, contribuindo para a construção e manutenção de um pipeline de financiamento no Brasil e/ou internacionalmente.

  • Será especialmente valorizada uma trajetória que demonstre conhecimento e compreensão do contexto amazônico, incluindo suas dinâmicas socioeconômicas, produtivas, ambientais, políticas e territoriais.

  • Será um diferencial experiência com mecanismos financeiros, finanças estruturadas, setor privado ou desenvolvimento econômico, especialmente quando aplicada a desafios socioambientais e/ou territoriais.

    Conhecimento e habilidades

  • Visão sistêmica da Amazônia: capacidade de compreender o território para além de uma única agenda temática, conectando desenvolvimento socioeconômico, conservação, produção agropecuária, floresta, clima, povos e comunidades tradicionais, políticas públicas e investimentos.

  • Pensamento estratégico e de escala: capacidade de identificar as principais alavancas de transformação de um sistema e desenvolver soluções que possam avançar de iniciativas pontuais para resultados de maior escala.

  • Gestão e implementação: capacidade de transformar estratégia em execução, estabelecer prioridades, acompanhar resultados e replanejar recursos e ações diante de mudanças de contexto.

  • Articulação e negociação: habilidade para navegar entre interesses distintos, construir agendas comuns e mobilizar atores públicos, privados e sociais em torno de objetivos compartilhados.

  • Visão econômico-financeira: capacidade de compreender o papel de investimentos, mecanismos financeiros, setor privado e modelos econômicos na construção de soluções sustentáveis para a Amazônia.

  • Captação e mobilização de recursos: habilidade para desenvolver relações com financiadores, identificar oportunidades e contribuir estrategicamente para a sustentabilidade financeira do portfólio.

  • Inglês avançado, oral e escrito, considerando as interações, apresentações e eventos internacionais inerentes à posição. Inglês fluente é desejável e conhecimentos de espanhol serão considerados um diferencial.

Competências

  • Visão sistêmica e pensamento estratégico: conecta diferentes variáveis e agendas, compreende interdependências e mantém uma visão ampla do território sem perder a capacidade de priorização.

  • Orientação à implementação e resultados: transforma estratégia em ação, acompanha a execução e mantém foco consistente nas entregas e no impacto esperado.

  • Liderança adaptativa: lidera com segurança em contextos de incerteza e complexidade, sendo capaz de rever planos, redirecionar prioridades e mobilizar o time diante de mudanças.

  • Influência e construção de consensos: estabelece relações de confiança e consegue aproximar atores com interesses e perspectivas distintas.

  • Liderança de pessoas: desenvolve equipes fortes e tecnicamente qualificadas, compartilha contexto, promove autonomia e evita a formação de silos na tomada de decisão.

  • Colaboração e integração: consegue navegar por um portfólio diverso sem precisar ser especialista em todas as temáticas, conectando conhecimentos, pessoas e iniciativas para gerar sinergias.

  • Proatividade e senso de protagonismo: antecipa necessidades, identifica oportunidades e mobiliza recursos e pessoas para fazer a estratégia avançar.

  • Compromisso com diversidade, equidade e inclusão: incorpora essa agenda à forma de liderar, desenvolver equipes e construir uma cultura organizacional inclusiva.

Perfil de nossa equipe

A The Nature Conservancy é enraizada em nossa missão e guiada por nossos valores. Temos o compromisso de cultivar um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo, onde todos os colegas ao redor do mundo sintam um senso de pertencimento e tenham suas contribuições únicas valorizadas. Nosso objetivo é construir uma força de trabalho diversa que reflita as comunidades em que atuamos, reconhecendo que a diversidade de experiências e habilidades é fundamental para a inovação.

“Você vai se juntar a nós pela nossa missão — e vai ficar pelas nossas pessoas.”

Principais interesses para trabalhar conosco

O candidato ideal será motivado pela oportunidade de causar um impacto direto nos esforços globais de conservação.

Deve ter um forte interesse em sustentabilidade ambiental, proteção da biodiversidade e conservação de ecossistemas críticos no Brasil.

Razões para se juntar à nossa equipe

  • A oportunidade de liderar uma estratégia de alta relevância para um dos biomas mais importantes para a biodiversidade e estabilidade climática global.

  • Atuação sobre desafios complexos que conectam desenvolvimento econômico, produção sustentável, conservação, clima, comunidades e políticas públicas.

  • Liderança de um portfólio diversificado e de uma equipe multidisciplinar em uma organização de alcance global.

  • Possibilidade de articular governos, setor privado, investidores, financiadores, comunidades e sociedade civil em torno de mudanças sistêmicas.

  • Espaço para construir soluções que ultrapassem projetos-piloto e alcancem escala e transformação de sistemas.

Detalhes relevantes antes de se candidatar a esta vaga

A posição exige residência fixa em uma capital da Amazônia Brasileira, em modelo home office. Também requer disponibilidade para viagens nacionais e internacionais e atuação eventual em locais remotos e condições climáticas ou de terreno desafiadoras.

Seeking Telemedicine Family/Internal Medicine Providers

Circle Medical is an adult-only primary care practice committed to the empanelment of primary care providers resulting in high quality, continuity of care for our patients through a telemedicine-first approach. We are an evidence-based practice that leverages our proprietary, HIPAA-compliant EHR that ensures a delightful and safe experience for patients and providers via two-way, video-audio appointments.
Please find out more about us on our website.

Pay is a fee-for-service model. Fully empaneled MD/DOs earn an average of $100/hr or $200/hr, respectively, with appointments lasting from 15 to 30 mins. MDs/DOs compensation is $50 per encounter, plus a robust incentive program. Fully empaneled NPs earn an average of $66/hr to $132/hr. NPs compensation is $33 per encounter.

*** Applicants must reside in the United States of America.

We deliver a true Primary Care Experience rooted in provider empanelment and continuity of care

We are a 7-day-a-week operation offering PCPs the freedom to set their own recurring schedules within any combination of days, including evenings and weekends.

PCPs are also supported by a strong team of patient care advocates and a licensed medical team who work with you to ensure our patients get the care and follow-up they need. We require a high degree of technical skill utilizing software and an open mind to fast-paced improvements driven by our product and engineering teams. We are in network with most PPO insurance plans and help our patients understand their coverage so that providers can focus on what is most important.

Education & licenses required for this position

  • Completed an accredited medical program with a national certification
  • Currently licensed in Pennsylvania
  • Valid Pennsylvania DEA Registration in good standing with all schedules to prescribe medications, including S2
  • Ideal candidates will have experience as primary care providers in a clinical setting
  • At least 3 years post-residency practice experience is strongly preferred for NP/APRNs
  • At least 2 years post-residency practice experience is strongly preferred for Physicians
  • Must be Board Certified in Family or Internal Medicine
  • Commitment to evidence-based medicine
  • Willingness to learn how to diagnose and treat a variety of adult/primary care conditions
  • A PC with Windows 11 Pro or a Mac newer than 2021 is required
Salary: $66 – $200 / hour

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: A Note on LevelsWe are hiring for two levels with this posting: Senior Software Engineer (P4) and Staff Software Engineer (P5).
jobs.description:
A Note on Levels

We are hiring for two levels with this posting: Senior Software Engineer (P4) and Staff Software Engineer (P5). The initial stages of this process include a recruiter screen, followed by a hiring manager interview. The hiring manager then determines the level after that conversation based on demonstrated experience and scope.

If you’re unsure which level fits you, apply anyway. We’d rather have that conversation with you than have you self-select out.

Who We Are

At Murmuration, we believe that America's promise is shaped and reshaped by the best ideas and ideals of its communities, and the dreams of the people who believe in a better life for themselves, their families, and each other.

We help organizations build power in their communities in four key ways: we organize a network of values-aligned partners; we provide deep, data-driven insights into people, places, and perspectives; we develop tools that make organizing and engagement easy and more effective; and we offer services that strengthen our partners' capacity to lead change in their communities.

We envision an America where every community has what it needs to help people lead healthy, free, and dignified lives. We work to redesign the systems and structures we all depend on — how we learn, live, govern, and solve problems — so that they are just, equitable, resilient, and rooted in shared responsibility. By strengthening the ties that hold communities together, we aim for civic life defined by collective action and care, with effective leadership that truly represents everyone.

We are a collaborative, curious, and creative team of organizers, scientists, teachers, technologists, campaign veterans, and more who share the unwavering belief that we can use our gifts in service of transforming America — together.

We've built our team guided by the belief that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. And so we support each other relentlessly — rallying together to face challenges the same way we celebrate each other's wins.

About the Position

Do you see yourself as a mission-driven engineer who believes that great products emerge from strong teams? Do you thrive in inclusive, thoughtful environments where engineers hold themselves to high standards of technical excellence, ownership, and impact at scale?

We are seeking a Senior or Staff Software Engineer to contribute to one of our most ambitious efforts: building a new product from the ground up while raising the bar for how our entire engineering organization works.

Murmuration builds technology that helps our partner organizations strengthen civic engagement and organize more effectively in their communities. Our products weave together engagement, outreach, demographic, and voter data with intuitive applications that help partners better understand and act within the communities they serve. Our team is intentionally multidisciplinary and partner-focused. We succeed together by aligning planning, execution, and learning across engineering, product, design, research, data, and partner success. We build complex, data-driven systems that need to work reliably during critical moments, scale as our partners grow, and remain understandable and maintainable as communities and their needs evolve.

As a Senior or Staff Software Engineer, you will join the Explorer Team as we evolve the product into general availability from its pilot implementation. Explorer is a data visualization product that facilitates political data exploration using interactive maps, charts, and exportable tables, supplemented by an NLP-powered search function.

On this small, close-knit team, you will establish the engineering patterns, operational foundations, and testing strategies needed to evolve Explorer into a secure, reliable, GA-ready platform. You and the team will build Explorer’s core platform and user experience, expanding a near-greenfield code base to design, build, and evolve secure backend services, interactive data visualizations, and responsive user interfaces. You will also produce high-quality documentation that improves knowledge sharing, onboarding, and the long-term maintainability of the product.

In addition to your Explorer work, you will serve as a senior technical resource across multiple projects, applying your expertise to solving some of the organization’s most complex challenges.

This role is suited for a deeply experienced individual contributor whose technical judgment and engineering rigor raises the quality of deliverables across the entire organization. You excel in near-greenfield settings where product priorities and direction can shift rapidly. Your commitment to building inclusive, high-trust, high-performing teams is visible across the technology organization. And you believe, like we do, that how we build is just as important as what we build.

What You’ll Do

Drive to General Availability

  • Shape Explorer's technical future: advise on technical priorities, dependencies, and complexity; propose and defend well-reasoned solutions with clear documentation of tradeoffs and alternatives;
  • Take a pilot implementation from limited release to general availability, including making early architectural decisions, validating technical assumptions, and iterating toward a scalable design;
  • Harden experimental systems for production readiness, including reliability, performance, observability, testing, and operational excellence;
  • Architect for the long term: design and build the systems and architectures that will serve Explorer for years, with scale, reliability, security, and maintainability as first-class concerns;
  • Improve and expand the existing code base: reinforce secure coding practices, identify vulnerabilities early, and treat data privacy and access control as first-class concerns;
  • Drive test strategy, proactively identify and address technical risks, and drive quality improvements at the team level; and
  • Reduce technical debt, improve system quality, and contribute to objectives that span the broader organization.

Elevate the Team

  • Resolve ambiguity, navigate requirements that are actively being shaped, and bring structure and clarity without waiting for perfect specs;
  • Establish best practices for test strategy, code quality, and system design; raise the technical bar across the organization through documentation, advocacy, and role modeling;
  • Mentor senior engineers and help emerging technical leads build the judgment, ownership, and skills to grow; lead technical discussions, drive design consensus, and model the standards you expect from others; and
  • Be like Ted Lasso: believe, build trust, and demonstrate kindness, empathy, optimism, curiosity, and vulnerability.

Lead Beyond Explorer

  • Set technical direction across teams beyond Explorer; own objectives that span multiple teams and align with division and organizational goals; drive the strategy, planning, decision-making, and execution needed to achieve them;
  • Lead significant initiatives spanning multiple teams and systems; align technical and non-technical stakeholders, communicate tradeoffs and risks clearly, and represent engineering in cross-organizational discussions and with product and leadership;
  • Champion secure coding practices at a systemic level, identify vulnerabilities across the product, and treat data privacy and access control as organization-wide concerns; and
  • Organize and lead incident response, involving the right people and delegating effectively; lead post-incident reviews including root cause analysis and clear prevention action items; follow through until learnings are shared and remediation is complete.

Note: The scope and organizational reach of “Lead Beyond Explorer” work will differ by level. At the Senior level, this means owning significant cross-team technical work and contributing to broader organizational decisions. At the Staff level, this means setting technical direction and leading multi-team initiatives with full organizational accountability.

Requirements

Technical Depth and Judgement

  • Deep, hands-on expertise across critical technical domains with the proven ability to lead system design, architectural patterns, and engineering best practices; your sound technical judgment shapes important decisions;
  • Experience with event-driven and asynchronous processing patterns; solid understanding of the tradeoffs among different event-driven architectures with the ability to defend one choice over the other;
  • Ability to reason across OLAP and OLTP data architectures and make sound design decisions for the systems that depend on them;
  • Comfort making sound decisions with imperfect information; able to design long-term architectures with scale, reliability, security, and maintainability as first-class concerns, and to clearly articulate tradeoffs and alternatives explored;
  • Ability to communicate and defend well-reasoned solutions through written documentation, sharing context, what alternatives were considered, and how conclusions were reached;
  • Be a proactive steward of technical quality, identifying and prioritizing technical debt, defining test strategy, and evaluating risk from bugs and architectural problems before they become blockers; and
  • Skill at debugging the most complex problems at any level of the stack; ability to drive effective post-incident reviews with clear timelines, root cause analysis, and actionable prevention plans.

Scope, Initiative, and Execution

  • Proven ability to lead technical strategy and execution for significant initiatives spanning multiple teams or systems, balancing quality, performance, and cost while keeping stakeholders aligned on tradeoffs and risks;
  • Proven experience in designing objectives aligned with division and organizational goals, anticipating technical challenges and proposing solutions before they become blockers;
  • Demonstrated experience in the estimation of large, cross-team projects with significant unknowns, including mitigation plans for resolving those unknowns, breaking work into milestones and iterations to reduce risk and deliver incremental value;
  • Proven strategies to involve the right people, delegate clearly, communicate consistently, and follow through as an owner until an objective is delivered; and
  • Ability to multiply team and engineering effectiveness through technical leadership, tooling, infrastructure, and process improvements.

Organizational Impact

  • A technical leader across multiple teams who can act without direct management responsibilities, influencing outcomes through role modeling, documentation, and advocacy rather than authority;
  • Demonstrated track record as a mentor to senior engineers with a proven ability to develop future technical leaders, building their judgment, ownership, and skills through 1:1 guidance and small-group knowledge sharing;
  • A driver of standards and best practices that raise the technical bar across the organization, creating processes that instill ownership behavior in others;
  • Ability to represent engineering effectively in cross-functional discussions, leading alignment across technical and non-technical stakeholders on complex, multi-team initiatives; and
  • A leader by example, proactively sharing context and learnings, building POCs or prototypes where most cost-effective, and creating the kind of high-trust, high-performing team culture that makes everyone better.

What You Bring to the Table

Foundations

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience with demonstrated full-stack fluency and a track record of delivering in production across a variety of languages and technology stacks;
  • Experience taking a product from beta to general availability, navigating the operational, quality, and cross-functional demands of a production launch;
  • Experience driving secure coding practices, data privacy principles, and access control patterns as applied in production systems;
  • A test-driven mindset with experience writing, maintaining, and driving test strategy at the team or product level;
  • A track record of effective collaboration with product, data science, and R&D teams, bridging technical and domain-specific perspectives across disciplines.

Data

  • Solid foundation in relational databases, including PostgreSQL, writing fluent SQL, designing schemas, and reasoning about migrations and query performance;
  • Experience with analytical or columnar datastores (e.g., Apache Pinot, ClickHouse, BigQuery, etc.);
  • Experience working with modern data warehousing and transformation workflows powered by Snowflake and dbt;
  • Experience with data pipeline orchestration tools such as Dagster or Airflow with an understanding of scheduling, dependency management, and pipeline reliability;
  • Working knowledge of time series data modeling and its applications;
  • Experience with caching layers such as Redis and the ability to drive decisions about caching strategy as part of system design.

Infrastructure and Observability

  • Deep experience with cloud-native architectures, distributed systems, and production-grade software at scale; production experience with AWS, including services for compute, storage, and observability;
  • Proficiency with Docker, Make, or similar build tools, as well as environment scripting;
  • Direct experience with observability tooling: logging, metrics, and tracing using tools such as Datadog, New Relic, Prometheus, or Grafana.

Security

  • Experience driving secure coding practices, data privacy principles, and access control patterns as applied in production systems.

Emerging and Specialized

  • Hands-on experience integrating LLM or AI APIs (e.g., OpenAI) into production applications, including working with embeddings, retrieval, or natural language interfaces;
  • Experience with geospatial or map-based data visualization and related JavaScript libraries.

Nice to Haves

  • Familiarity with Voter File Data;
  • Experience with or interest in political data;
  • Background in political tech, civic tech, advocacy, or mission-driven organizations; and/or
  • Experience applying AI/ML techniques to voter or political data.

Talented Software Engineers come from all walks of life and career. If you are passionate about civic engagement and technology, please apply, even if you do not check every box!

Benefits

Location and Compensation

This is a full-time, salaried position with a comprehensive benefits package, open to candidates anywhere in the United States. Respective starting salaries below:

Senior Software Engineer (P4): $190,576

Staff Software Engineer (P5): $225,324

We set compensation using market data and apply it consistently across the organization to ensure fairness and transparency for everyone in similar roles.

Our Culture of Care

We work hard to create a culture of care to ensure that our staff are best equipped to lead happy, healthy, and balanced lives. To that end, we offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes:

  • Health, vision, and dental insurance with 100% of premiums covered for you and qualifying family members;
  • Retirement benefits with a 5% employer match;
  • A flexible unlimited PTO plan;
  • Generous paid parental leave;
  • Pre-tax commuter benefits;
  • A company laptop;
  • A flexible remote work environment;
  • A home office setup stipend for all new employees;
  • Monthly reimbursement for remote work expenses;
  • A yearly professional development fund;
  • Mental health and wellness benefits through Calm and Better Help;
  • Yearly in-person staff retreats; and
  • A welcoming culture that celebrates diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.

At Murmuration, we believe a vibrant, representative democracy depends on the inclusion of diverse voices, lived experiences, and perspectives. The best ideas don’t come from a single person or ideology — they emerge at the intersection of different backgrounds, identities, and viewpoints. We are proud of our commitment to building an organization and culture shaped by respect, empathy, and collaboration, where our team’s diversity fuels innovation, civic engagement, and meaningful change. We welcome new colleagues who will help us nurture this collective effort. Join us.

An Equal-Opportunity Employer with a Commitment to Diversity

Murmuration is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and as an organization committed to diversity and the perspective of all voices, we consider applicants equally of race, gender, color, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, disability, political affiliation and national origin. We reasonably accommodate staff members and/or applicants with disabilities, provided they are otherwise able to perform the essential functions of the job.

Note: Murmuration is two organizations working together to pursue our mission of amplifying the power of civic engagement: Murmuration Research Institute, a 501(c)(3) that conducts research to identify, design, and create the data, tools, and insights that build healthier and more equitable communities; and Murmuration, Inc., a 501(c)(4) that supports organizations working across the country on the nation’s most challenging issues with access to data, tools, and research that build healthier and more equitable communities.

At Feeld, we are creating a world where everyone is more intimately connected to each other and themselves. We are building an inclusive, human-centered product and are looking for a VP of Growth to become part of our remote team and our mission to elevate the human experience of sexuality and relationships.

We’re looking for a seasoned, full-stack growth leader to own and evolve our growth engine across performance marketing, lifecycle, and CRM. This role is not about optimizing channels in isolation or chasing short-term gains. It’s about building a sustainable, compounding growth system—one that deepens the strength of our network, sharpens our brand, and creates meaningful long-term value.

You’re a seasoned leader in driving growth in complex consumer environments, with a track record of scaling responsibly. You’re highly analytical, but not led by data alone. You combine rigor with intuition, curiosity, and a strong sensitivity to brand and member experience.

You will operate at the intersection of marketing, product, and data, connecting acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention into a cohesive system. You think in loops, not funnels. You care as much about how we grow as how fast we grow.

What you will do:

  • Define and lead the growth strategy across performance marketing and lifecycle, ensuring values-aligned member acquisition to support the long-term health and integrity of the Feeld experience at scale
  • Own the performance marketing ecosystem end-to-end: channel strategy, account structure, budget allocation, and scaling frameworks
  • Build and drive a rigorous experimentation roadmap, establishing a culture of testing across channels, creative, messaging, and lifecycle journeys
  • Audit and evolve existing channels, identifying inefficiencies and opportunities, while incubating and scaling new channels through structured testing
  • Design and integrate lifecycle and performance systems, ensuring seamless handoffs between acquisition, activation, retention, and re-engagement
  • Develop a product-led growth lens, partnering closely with Product to unlock growth through onboarding, engagement loops, and core member experiences
  • Drive referral and network effects initiatives, creating programs that compound growth through user advocacy and community dynamics
  • Establish clear measurement frameworks, balancing incrementality, LTV, and payback with broader signals of network health and brand strength
  • Build and lead a high-performing growth team, spanning performance, lifecycle, and analytics, while fostering cross-functional collaboration
  • Champion the brand within growth, ensuring all acquisition and lifecycle efforts reinforce—not erode—the brand and member experience

Requirements

About you:

  • 10+ years of experience in growth leadership, with a proven track record of scaling consumer businesses across performance marketing and lifecycle
  • Deep experience in DTC and/or subscription models, with a strong understanding of LTV, retention dynamics, and unit economics; marketplace or social experience a significant plus
  • Fluent across multiple altitudes—able to move seamlessly from high-level strategy and planning to hands-on execution and problem-solving
  • Entrepreneurial and highly resourceful, with a scrappy, can-do mindset and a bias toward action in fast-moving environments
  • Comfortable with ambiguity, with the ability to create structure, clarity, and momentum in undefined or evolving problem spaces
  • Strong expertise in attribution and incrementality, with a nuanced understanding of measurement limitations and how to make decisions despite them
  • Excellent communicator and cross-functional leader, able to align teams across marketing, product, and data while advocating for both growth and brand integrity

Benefits

About us:

Feeld is an independent, experimental and fully remote organisation reshaping the dialogue on dating and sexuality. The company was founded in 2014 and has evolved since to become the open, distributed structure it is now. We have a naturally agile and fluid culture. The whole team is fully remote, which means you work where and when helps you perform at your best. We regard autonomy highly and treat our organisation as a product – we iterate, improve and test things internally to see what works best for everyone.

Our culture:

We believe in creating a safe work environment through humanity, fluidity, safety, transparency and progressiveness. When hiring, we look for culture add rather than culture fit.

Because we are a fully remote team, it’s especially important that we create an environment where our colleagues feel included and connected as humans.

Diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging at Feeld:

Feeld promotes open-mindedness, inclusion, diversity and kindness, both in the world and among our own workforce.

We encourage and welcome applications from people with a history of marginalisation, whether because of race, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, neurodivergence, national origin, disability (seen or unseen) or any confluence of intersectional identities.

Our goal is a barrier-free application process and working environment. If you require further details or assistance or have any questions about this process, please let us know at .

Compensation and perks:

We are conscious of how our work and decisions impact other humans and the environment. We design our product and organisation with consideration for the wellbeing of our Members and colleagues. Feeld’s way of working is designed to proactively prevent burnout and an “always on” culture. We believe in technology and working environments that enable people to live a meaningful, fulfilled life.

Therefore, we offer our staff:

  • Flexible working hours
  • Unlimited paid time off
  • A fully remote working situation
  • Home office budget
  • Learning & development budget
  • On demand therapy sessions and mental health support via Spill
  • In-person meet ups

Our compensation system is one of the ways we work to uphold equity and inclusion at Feeld. Just as we strive to enable honest expression on our platform, we strive for openness of information within the organization. Internally, we keep decision-making transparent to keep each other accountable and make sure all voices are heard. That is why we offer a compensation system that is transparent, honest, and equitable. Additionally, we believe all humans deserve to earn a competitive wage, so we offer a Baseline Freedom Salary of £60,000 GBP per year for any role that indexes below £60,000 GBP per year.

Estimated compensation for this role:

  • Total cash compensation for this role varies by geographic location. We estimate the market-competitive compensation range for this position to be between $210,000 - $290,000 USD.

Our interview process:

  • Your first conversation with Feeld will be a screening call with our recruiter, where you’ll be able to ask - and receive answers - regarding any general questions you have and to confirm the role is a fit for what you’re seeking.
  • Your second conversation will connect you directly with the hiring manager for the role you’re applying to. Here, you’ll have a chance to ask more questions about the work you’ll be doing. This conversation will also focus on your past work experiences.
  • The next step for most of our roles is a candidate challenge. This is an evaluation of the skills relevant to be successful in this role and generally takes about an hour to complete.
  • Your third conversation allows you the opportunity to meet the team members you might be working with on a daily basis. Here, you’ll be able to ask questions about team processes, workflow, and the employee experience at Feeld.
  • We generally make an offer within 2 weeks of our final call, and offer a flexible start date that can begin as early as the next Monday after you sign our offer documentation.
  • Of note: all of our interviews are conducted remotely, and our interviewers will work with you to find an agreeable interview time based on mutual availability.

We understand we're asking you to invest your time and best efforts in our process, and are appreciative of getting the chance to better know who you are as a person and candidate. In return, we’re committed to offering transparent communication and prompt feedback as you navigate this application with us.

Job Overview

We are seeking a highly experienced Senior Linux Infrastructure Engineer with deep expertise in Linux administration, bare metal infrastructure, enterprise storage, and next-generation AI Factory / GPU infrastructure platforms. This role is focused on designing, deploying, operating, and troubleshooting large-scale Linux-based infrastructure that powers both traditional enterprise workloads and modern AI/ML environments.

This is not a DevOps-focused role. We already have a dedicated DevOps team and are looking for an engineer with extensive hands-on experience in Bare Metal as a Service (BMaaS), GPU infrastructure, high-performance storage, data center operations, and enterprise Linux platforms.

The ideal candidate will have experience building and managing infrastructure from the hardware layer up, including servers, networking, storage, GPU clusters, and AI-ready platforms. They should be comfortable working with high-performance computing (HPC), AI Factory environments, and large-scale Linux deployments where performance, reliability, and operational excellence are critical.

Key Responsibilities & Required Skills

Linux & Bare Metal Infrastructure

  • Expert-level Linux administration (Ubuntu required; Red Hat and SUSE preferred)
  • Deep expertise in bare metal server deployment, architecture, provisioning, and lifecycle management
  • Experience operating Bare Metal as a Service (BMaaS) platforms and large-scale infrastructure environments
  • Strong understanding of server hardware, including:
    • BIOS/UEFI
    • RAID controllers
    • Firmware management
    • iLO/iDRAC/IPMI
    • NICs and SmartNICs
    • HBA cards
    • Hardware diagnostics and troubleshooting
  • Experience designing, implementing, and supporting enterprise Linux infrastructure at scale

AI Factory & GPU Infrastructure

  • Experience deploying and managing GPU-accelerated infrastructure for AI/ML workloads
  • Understanding of NVIDIA GPU technologies including:
    • A100, H100, H200, B200, or equivalent GPU platforms
    • NVIDIA DGX and OEM GPU servers
    • GPU provisioning and lifecycle management
    • GPU monitoring and performance optimization
  • Knowledge of AI Factory architecture and infrastructure requirements
  • Experience supporting GPU clusters, AI training environments, and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads
  • Understanding of:
    • GPU resource allocation and scheduling
    • Multi-GPU systems
    • GPU networking requirements
    • High-bandwidth, low-latency infrastructure design
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA ecosystem technologies such as:
    • CUDA
    • NCCL
    • GPUDirect Storage
    • NVIDIA Fabric Manager
    • NVIDIA Base Command (preferred)

Enterprise Storage & Data Platforms

  • Advanced Linux storage administration:
    • LVM
    • XFS, EXT4
    • NFS
    • iSCSI
    • Fibre Channel SAN
    • Multipath I/O
  • Strong hands-on experience with Ceph, including:
    • Cluster architecture
    • MON, OSD, MDS
    • RBD, CephFS, RGW
    • Capacity planning
    • Performance tuning
    • Failure recovery
  • Experience with high-performance AI storage platforms such as:
    • WEKA
    • VAST Data
    • Dell PowerScale
    • Pure Storage FlashBlade
    • NetApp
  • Understanding of:
    • NVMe-over-Fabrics (NVMe-oF)
    • RDMA
    • GPUDirect Storage
    • Parallel file systems
    • AI data pipelines

Networking & Infrastructure

  • Strong networking knowledge:
    • Bonding
    • VLANs
    • Routing
    • MTU optimization
    • DNS
    • DHCP
  • Experience with high-performance data center networking:
    • 100G/200G/400G Ethernet
    • RoCE
    • RDMA
    • Spine-Leaf architectures
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA Spectrum-X, Mellanox/NVIDIA ConnectX adapters, or equivalent technologies
  • Strong understanding of Layer 2 and Layer 3 infrastructure design and troubleshooting

Operations & Reliability

  • Experience with high availability, clustering, and disaster recovery
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across:
    • Linux operating systems
    • Hardware platforms
    • GPU infrastructure
    • Networking
    • Enterprise storage
  • Experience supporting mission-critical production environments
  • Bash and Python scripting for automation and operational efficiency
  • Experience creating operational documentation, runbooks, and infrastructure standards

Nice to Have

  • Kubernetes infrastructure (especially AI/ML and GPU integration)
  • KVM, VMware, OpenShift Virtualization, or similar virtualization platforms
  • Ansible automation
  • NVIDIA Base Command Manager
  • Slurm or HPC workload schedulers
  • Observability and monitoring platforms (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)
  • Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) tools
  • IPAM solutions
  • AWS, Azure, or hybrid cloud exposure

We Are Not Looking For

  • Candidates whose experience is primarily CI/CD pipeline engineering
  • Engineers focused mainly on Terraform, GitOps, or application delivery pipelines
  • Cloud-only administrators with limited bare metal, storage, or hardware experience
  • Professionals whose primary expertise is software development rather than infrastructure engineering

Ideal Candidate

Someone who has spent years designing, building, and operating enterprise Linux environments, large-scale bare metal infrastructure, storage platforms, and modern AI Factory environments. The ideal candidate understands how to deploy and manage GPU-enabled infrastructure, BMaaS platforms, enterprise storage, and high-performance networking while solving complex operating system, hardware, storage, and AI infrastructure challenges. DevOps experience is a plus, but deep Linux, infrastructure, storage, BMaaS, and AI Factory expertise is the primary requirement.

Why Bixal?

Bixal is a consulting company headquartered in Fairfax, VA, working alongside governments and organizations to help them deliver better services and experiences to the communities they serve. Using evidence-based knowledge and technology, Bixal empowers clients to deliver on their missions more effectively by fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement.

Our values:

  • People-First: Emphasizing the importance of people in all aspects of work.

  • Collaboration and Transparency: Valuing teamwork and open communication.

  • Growth Mindset: Encouraging innovation and continuous improvement.

  • Creating Lasting Impact: Focusing on meaningful outcomes and positive change.

About the role:

Bixal is seeking a Knowledge Management Specialist, Digital Support Operations to help keep a large public-facing federal digital program running smoothly and well documented. You will provide Tier 2 support across a portfolio of websites and applications, manage the queue where program questions and issues arrive, document the business processes the support operation runs on, and establish the process for communicating with users when a service is disrupted. It suits someone who would rather fix the process that generated fifty tickets than close them one at a time.

The program supports a large and diverse community through a broad portfolio of public websites, applications, and learning platforms. When a program question comes in, an interface breaks, or a service goes down, the quality of the response depends on the processes, documentation, and knowledge behind the support operation.

This project supports a large-scale outreach and engagement effort, delivering strategic communications, content and creative services, digital strategy, and audience engagement across public-facing websites, applications, and social media platforms. The work is paired with the IT, cybersecurity, and data operations needed to keep that digital presence secure, reliable, and available around the clock. The program's mission is to ensure the intended audience receives timely, accurate, and accessible information about the programs, services, and policies that affect them with content and platforms built to scale, adapt to changing needs, and hold up to federal compliance and security standards.

This is a full-time position contingent on contract award by our client, with a defined performance period of one year with two one-year option periods. This role offers you a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact on a project that aligns with Bixal’s mission of delivering innovative, human-centered solutions. While the role has a fixed duration, we are committed to transparency and collaboration, keeping you informed about contract updates and new opportunities. At Bixal, we support your professional journey, ensuring your experience reflects our inclusive, purpose-driven culture and prepares you for future success.

Location

This role can work remotely from anywhere in the USA. You must be legally authorized to work in the US.  Bixal does not provide visa sponsorship.

Compensation:

The salary range for this role is $77,000 – $87,000. In the spirit of transparency, most offers tend to land near the midpoint of the range. We make compensation decisions thoughtfully, considering your experience, the skills you bring, and our commitment to internal equity. Fairness and transparency are core to how we operate.

Responsibilities:

Support & Service Operations

  • Provide Tier 2 support for online resources, website/interface issues, and program questions.

  • Manage the user request and inquiry queue, including acknowledgment, routing, tracking, and closure.

  • Monitor key digital pages, tools, and functions daily and escalate issues.

Process & Knowledge Management

  • Train staff to submit, use, and maintain knowledge and content.

  • Perform technical editing and proofreading against program standards, AP style, and federal plain-language requirements.

  • Coordinate with information architecture and search specialists on metadata, categorization, retrieval, reuse, tracking, and routing.

  • Contribute to digital publishing operations, including the editorial calendar, recurring publications/newsletters, subscriptions, and audits.

  • Partner with search specialists on staff education around search, findability, and content standards.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

  • Build and maintain the Tier 2 customer support satisfaction dashboard.

  • Analyze recurring issues, trends, and topics.

  • Translate support data into process improvements and self-service content.

  • Other relevant duties as qualified/trained to perform

Qualifications:

  • Active Secret clearance. An interim Secret is acceptable to start.

  • Bachelor's degree, or equivalent professional experience.

  • At least 4 years in knowledge management, technical writing, documentation development, content operations, or customer support operations.

  • Hands-on experience with an enterprise knowledge base, documentation platform, or content management system.

  • Experience providing tiered customer or program support, working to defined acknowledgment and routing timeframes with a ticketing or case management system, and familiarity with ITIL practices for knowledge management, incident, problem and change.

  • Experience documenting business processes and standard operating procedures used by an operational team.

  • Experience with incident or service-disruption communications — the processes, severity definitions and notice templates that govern how users are told something is broken.

  • Demonstrated ability to draw knowledge out of subject-matter experts, interviewing program and technical staff and turning what they know into documentation someone else can follow.

  • ITIL v4 Foundation certification, or willingness to obtain it within 90 days of start.
